title: COA questions Cebu government’s ‘heavy reliance’ on job order workers in 2025
summary: COA says in its audit report that the Cebu provincial government had a total of 2,918 job order hires in 2025, or 68.24% of its total workforce that year

blocks.text: COA. The Commission on Audit in Commonwealth Avenue, Quezon City.
COA says in its audit report that the Cebu provincial government had a total of 2,918 job order hires in 2025, or 68.24% of its total workforce that year
MANILA, Philippines – The Commission on Audit (COA) has questioned the Cebu provincial government’s “heavy reliance” on job order (JO) workers in 2025.
COA said in its audit report that the Cebu provincial government had a total of 2,918 job order hires in 2025, or 68.24% of its total workforce of 4,276 that year.
It noted that in the same year, the Cebu government failed to fill up 1,789 vacancies in regular and casual positions.
The breakdown provided in the 2025 audit report showed the following:

items: Cebu Provincial Hospital (CPH)-Bogo City: 278 JOs vs 231 vacancies
Governor’s Office: 267 JOs vs 111 vacancies (including 67 permanent posts).

blocks.text: “This heavy reliance on JO workers, despite the substantial number of unfilled regular and casual positions, indicates possible non-compliance with civil service rules and undermines the efficient utilization of government human resources,” the COA said.

The state auditor reminded the Cebu provincial government of the Local Government Code provision requiring local government units to establish organizational structures and staffing patterns based on service requirements and financial capability, subject to applicable standards prescribed by the Civil Service Commission.

The COA and the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) earlier issued Joint Circular No. 2,. s of 2020 encouraging the priority hiring of qualified JO and contract of service personnel for unfilled plantilla positions.
Based on the COA’s count, 633 nurses were hired on JO basis even if there were 371 vacant posts.

JO workers also took professional and technical positions — nursing attendants, medical specialists, medical officers, midwives, and radiologic technologists — even when there were existing vacancies for these.

“The data indicate that a substantial number of professional and technical positions essential to hospital operations are being performed by JO workers while corresponding plantilla positions remain vacant. This arrangement reflects a mismatch between the approved staffing pattern and the actual workforce composition,” state auditors said.

While LGUs are authorized to tap JO workers when justified by operational requirements and available appropriations, such engagements should only complement the existing permanent workforce, rather than serving as substitute for the number of regular employees necessary to the delivery of government services.

Auditors also noted that while JO hires do not enjoy security of employment and do not enjoy standard benefits and entitlements of employees holding plantilla positions, they are nonetheless assigned to functions involving “professional, technical, and continuing services that are more closely aligned with plantilla or COS engagements.”

COA recommended that Cebu government undertake a comprehensive review of its staffing pattern to check the necessity of getting so many JO hires, and to prioritize the hiring of qualified JO workers for vacant positions.
In their response to the audit team, Cebu provincial officials informed COA that 42% of vacant permanent positions had been published, while 47 posts had been filled — 23 from JO hires.
The Provincial Human Resource and Management Officer also reported that there were 1,013 vacant permanent positions under review as end-2025, and that 66 already filled. – Rappler.com
